note: All results are from MuJoCo simulation of self-built rigid test articles. Calibration uses SYNTHETIC ground truth (a hidden perturbed model + sensor noise); the fitter's model class equals the generating class, so coverage is self-consistent and is NOT sim-to-real validation. No real vehicle is modelled or validated. Rule proposer walks a hand-written hypothesis list, so 'discovery' = the order evaluated and the keep/discard evidence. The LLM proposer is code only (off by default, never run). 'Human approval' of the hardware class is simulated by a dict entry.

excitation_entries.hypothesis: Add a single-thruster pulse (t0 only): net force AND torque, so mass/thrust-gain and COM-x separate from the pure couple.
Add a lateral thruster pulse (t4 only, +x force at z=+0.15): torque arm depends on COM-z.
Add a 2 m tilted drop onto the ground (no thrust): contact stiffness/damping and COM show up in the impact.
Add a coast with 3 m/s initial velocity: linear drag identifiable from decay.
Repeat the single-thruster pulse with a known +5 kg calibration mass: separates mass from thrust-gain (F/m vs gain/inertia).

roadster_scale.note: Same loop on a rigid 1300 kg box with thrusters at +-2.1 m (Roadster spike pitch-axis numbers; Iyy 2085 kg m^2). Not the Roadster template and not a real vehicle. Controller gains are in normalised-command units, so no retuning of the controller structure or bounds was needed; COM-offset disturbance was scaled x4.2 with body length.
